prose.title: Sex Manther Tagged McCaffrey, Threw Him Back, and Bought Lamar Jackson
prose.dek: Josh Martel cleared {{f.team.0007.cuts_s2_salary}} of salary before the auction lock, spent {{f.team.0007.top_buy_price}} of it on Lamar Jackson, and front-loaded Rashee Rice with what was left. The preseason simulation ranks Sex Manther {{f.team.0007.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was expensive. Martel carried {{f.team.0007.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0007.cap_opening}} in salary, with {{f.team.0007.studs_opening}} top-twelve starters: Caleb Williams, a High-end QB1, Christian McCaffrey and De'Von Achane at running back, and Harold Fannin and George Kittle at tight end. Rashee Rice was solid at receiver. The {{f.team.0007.holes_opening}} holes were Rome Odunze at the second receiver spot, Jacory Croskey-Merritt in a flex, and Jonathon Brooks, a running back, in the superflex.

The spring moves were all about picks. In March Martel sent 1.10 to Blake Bombers for their 2027 first, and in May he sent 3.04 and 3.06 to the Long Haulers for five later picks. No cuts, no extensions, and no rookie deals ran out on him.

t.0007.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: Then the chip. Martel tagged McCaffrey in May at {{f.team.0007.contract_13130_salary}}, which is what a tag is for in this league: something to trade, to keep, or to hand back. In July he handed it back, releasing McCaffrey with no penalty and taking every dollar of that {{f.team.0007.cut_13130_salary}} with him to spend on other people. C-Town ended up paying barely more than the tag for McCaffrey at the auction, which is exactly the trade-off Martel signed up for.

The rest of the room came fast. In June he extended Achane at {{f.team.0007.contract_16167_salary}} this year and Rice at {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_salary}}. In July Kittle and his {{f.team.0007.trade3_salary_out}} salary went to Blake Bombers with {{f.team.0007.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money for a 2027 second, Efton Chism went to Cleon Ca$h, and the day before the lock Martel cut Tyreek Hill, {{f.team.0007.cut_12801_salary}} of salary with a {{f.team.0007.cut_12801_penalty}} penalty. The draft, {{f.team.0007.rookie_picks_count}} picks from 3.11 down, was mostly defenders, and Sean Tucker came from the Expired Rookie Auction for {{f.team.0007.era_16166_price}}.

So the roster held at {{f.team.0007.active_roster_preauction}} active players while the salary fell from {{f.team.0007.cap_opening}} to {{f.team.0007.cap_preauction}}. McCaffrey, Hill and Kittle were the difference, and the room was the point.

t.0007.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: He opened a little more on the eve of the auction, restructuring Achane down to {{f.team.0007.contract_16167_salary_2}} for 2026, and then spent it. Lamar Jackson cost {{f.team.0007.faa_13593_price}} after twelve bids, Jaylen Waddle {{f.team.0007.faa_15284_price}} and Jameson Williams {{f.team.0007.faa_15756_price}}, part of {{f.team.0007.faa_spend}} across {{f.team.0007.faa_lots_won}} wins.

Jackson is the Elite in the What it bought column, Waddle and Williams the two Good buys, and the league table ranks the spending {{f.team.0007.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added and {{f.team.0007.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} for how much it added in all. With Caleb Williams in the superflex, his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0007.qb_rank|ord}} in the league.

The contracts that followed were long ones. Jackson signed for {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0007.contract_13593_tcv}} in all, Waddle for {{f.team.0007.contract_15284_tcv}} and Williams for {{f.team.0007.contract_15756_tcv}}. And the room left over after the auction did not go to waste: in September Martel restructured Rice, raising this year's number to {{f.team.0007.contract_16194_salary_2}} to push money out of the years ahead. He claimed {{f.team.0007.pickups_s3}} players off waivers before week one, released Tucker and a string of minimum bodies at no cost, and traded Gunnar Helm to the Long Haulers.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0007.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Jackson, Caleb Williams, Achane and Fannin, with Rice, Waddle and Jameson Williams solid at receiver, and {{f.team.0007.holes_today}} holes: Croskey-Merritt at the second running back spot and Odunze in a flex. The kicker, Eddy Pineiro, is replacement-level on MFL's projections, a footnote like the defense.

captions.t.0007.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Martel arrived in {{f.team.0007.hist_first_season}}, and in {{f.team.0007.hist_seasons}} seasons he has built one of the league's best records: back-to-back titles in {{f.team.0007.hist_title_years}}, runner-up in {{f.team.0007.hist_runner_up_years}}, {{f.team.0007.hist_div_titles}} division titles and {{f.team.0007.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips. His {{f.team.0007.hist_allplay_pct}} career all-play record is the second best in the league.

In Maddie Mondays the simulation has Sex Manther {{f.team.0007.power_rank|ord}}, one spot behind Real Deal Creel at {{f.league.power_rank_0008|ord}} and well clear of L.A. Looks at {{f.league.power_rank_0001|ord}}. That is a {{f.team.0007.sim_p_division}} chance at the division, {{f.team.0007.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and {{f.team.0007.sim_p_title}} title odds, with Creel and Bousquet five times each.

The next three years, Martel style. 2027: Lamar. Achane. Blake's first-round pick. The broom comes out 🧹 2028: a third title, if memory serves, which it never does. 2029: he concedes a big game early and graciously, reading his opponent's injury report aloud, and then wins it anyway.

Week one has started kindly: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Julian Love had an interception, Pineiro hit a long field goal, and Sex Manther has {{f.team.0007.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
